title: Smoked Mackerel Pâté
subtitle: Creamy smoked mackerel and cream cheese pâté
excerpt: Smoked mackerel fillets blended with cream cheese, horseradish, and lemon juice into a creamy, smoky pâté. Ready in 10 minutes and served with toast or oatcakes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Smoked mackerel pâté is a British classic, widely served as a starter or at informal buffets. Mackerel is one of Britain's most abundant and affordable fish, caught in large quantities around the coastline, and its cold-smoked form has a long shelf life and an intense, rich flavour. The pâté requires no cooking: the smoked fillets are simply blended or beaten with cream cheese, horseradish, lemon juice, and pepper into a rough or smooth paste according to preference. The horseradish is the traditional British accompaniment to mackerel, providing sharpness to cut the richness of the fish. The pâté can be prepared entirely by hand for a rougher, more textured result, or processed to a smooth cream. It keeps for up to three days in the fridge.

content.text: Remove the skin from the mackerel fillets and check carefully for bones before blending. The fillets should be at room temperature rather than cold from the fridge: room-temperature fish blends more smoothly and the flavour is more pronounced. Blend briefly for a rough, textured pâté or process longer for a smooth cream. The cream cheese provides richness; too much makes it stodgy. Taste carefully before serving: smoked mackerel varies significantly in its salt content depending on the producer and the length of smoking.
Remove the skin from the mackerel fillets and check for any remaining pin bones. Break the flesh into a food processor. Add the cream cheese, horseradish, lemon juice, and pepper.
Pulse to combine: briefly for a rough, textured result; longer for a smooth cream. Taste and adjust the lemon juice, horseradish, and pepper. The pâté should be punchy and well-seasoned.
Spoon into a serving dish or individual ramekins. Scatter with parsley. Serve immediately with hot toast, oatcakes, or sourdough, and lemon wedges for squeezing.
